solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bess's mate quietly quits unbridled love-in

indicators.note: the quiet letter quits, or leaves, the name of Bess's mate

parts.note: Porgy is Bess's partner in Gershwin's opera Porgy and Bess
P, piano, is the musical abbreviation for quietly

explanation.surface: A man walks out on his partner and an anything-goes party at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Porgy and Bess is Gershwin's folk opera; drop its hero's P (piano, quietly) to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy is a wild party with sexual licence, an unrestrained love-in.

clue.text: Stuff concerning payment given to duke

parts.note: over can mean about, concerning
a fee is a payment

explanation.surface: Matters of a fee handed to an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff someone is to give them too much food, to overfeed them.

clue.text: Jokes about juvenile Romeo's Sunday best

indicators.note: the word for jokes goes about, around, the boy and R

parts.note: gags are jokes
a lad is a youth
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Jokes concerning a young Romeo dressed in his finest clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags are informal for one's best clothes, worn for special occasions like Sunday church.

clue.text: Cheap product that reflects one snug home in river

indicators.note: one and a snug home are placed in the river's name

parts.note: the Rhone is a river of Switzerland and France
I is the Roman numeral one
a nest is a cosy home

explanation.surface: Some cheap glittery item mirroring a cosy house beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River' could be the Rhine, which is in the answer, but the wordplay needs the RHONE around INEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhinestone is an imitation diamond, a cheap glittering stone that catches the light.

clue.text: Former slave the Spanish must have smuggled outside

indicators.note: the word for smuggled sits outside the Spanish article

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen or smuggled goods
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A one-time slave Spaniards must have sneaked out of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: Helots were the serf class of ancient Sparta.
explanation.definitionFit: A helot was a state-owned serf in ancient Sparta, so a slave of former times.

clue.text: Old queen's new hat, half lowered, that is raised outside

indicators.note: the raised letters go around the altered hat
in a down clue raised means the letters read upwards

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is

indicators.note: the first half of the word for hat is lowered beneath its second half

parts.note: titfer is Cockney rhyming slang for hat (tit for tat)

explanation.surface: An ancient queen with a newly adjusted crown.
explanation.walkthrough: Titfer is Cockney rhyming slang (tit for tat) for a hat. 'Half lowered' drops its top half beneath the bottom half rather than reversing the whole word.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefertiti was an Egyptian queen, wife of the pharaoh Akhenaten, famous from her painted bust.

clue.text: Pole, Frenchman, colonist and soldier

parts.note: a staff is a pole or stick
Serge is a French man's name
ants live in colonies

explanation.surface: A list of nationalities and roles, like the start of a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' and 'Frenchman' look like nationalities; one is a stick, the other just a French first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff sergeant is a non-commissioned army officer, senior to a sergeant.

clue.text: After overture to opera I put in part for songster

indicators.note: the rest follows after the opening letter in the answer
the overture comes at the start, so take the opening letter of opera
the I is put into the word for part

parts.note: a role is an actor's part

explanation.surface: After the opera's overture, the singer is given a part.
explanation.walkthrough: Songster here means a songbird, not a singer.
explanation.definitionFit: An oriole is a bird known for its fluting song, a songster in the bird sense.

clue.text: Cross with one representative of this cricket side

definitions.text: Cross with one representative of this cricket side

parts.words: Cross with one representative of this cricket side
parts.note: a cross, X, is the Roman numeral ten; with I, one, it makes XI, the usual way to write a cricket team

explanation.walkthrough: A cricket team has eleven players, written XI in team listings: an X (cross) with I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket side, the team of players, is numbered and often called by that number.

clue.text: Gospel turns on church body

indicators.note: turns tells us to read the words for on and church body backwards

parts.note: on is the leg side in cricket, so on gives LEG
the nave is the main body of a church

explanation.surface: Gospel music is played to the congregation in church.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is also called the leg side, so on can give LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: An evangel is a gospel, especially one of the four New Testament books, from the Greek for good news.

clue.text: Agrees enough's converted into methane maybe

indicators.note: converted means the letters are changed into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone is persuaded that methane counts as something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' marks methane as one example of the category.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane traps heat in the atmosphere, one example of a gas causing global warming.

clue.text: Flimsy paper kept in folder

indicators.note: the word for paper is held inside the word for folder

parts.note: a file is a folder for papers
rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A delicate sheet of paper stored in a document folder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fragile is easily broken, delicate and weak like a flimsy object.

clue.text: Evergreen tree somehow hides each stage performer

parts.note: a fir is an evergreen conifer

indicators.note: the rearranged tree hides the short form of each within it
somehow says the letters of tree come out in some other arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An evergreen tree concealing something from each performer on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Evergreen tree' as one plant, but only 'Evergreen' gives the conifer; 'tree' is the fodder to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-eater is a circus or street entertainer who appears to swallow flames.

clue.text: Mock group running football at city university

parts.note: the FA, Football Association, runs English football
LSE, London School of Economics, a university in the City of London's neighbour

explanation.surface: Making fun of the football authorities meeting at a London university.
explanation.walkthrough: The LSE is the London School of Economics, part of the University of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Mock as an adjective means imitation or sham, so false in the sense of not genuine.

clue.text: Motor club's loco controller

parts.note: a motor is an engine
a driver is a golf club for long tee shots

explanation.surface: A motoring club's man in charge of a locomotive.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine driver operates a railway locomotive, the loco of the clue.

clue.text: Strip down poor piece finally about conservationists

indicators.note: the word for poor goes around the conservationists

parts.note: dismal can mean poor in quality
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage conservation charity

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of piece

explanation.surface: A shoddy item being taken apart, with talk of environmentalists.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust (NT) looks after historic houses and landscape in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle is to take apart, strip a machine down into components.

clue.text: Surfers enjoy this band

definitions.meaning: surfers ride a long breaking wave in the sea

explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads as the sea; the second is the radio band once used by stations such as BBC Radio 4.
explanation.definitionFit: Long wave is the range of radio frequencies below medium wave, and literally a lengthy roller in the sea.

clue.text: Outline Klee's absurdly fashionable style

indicators.note: absurdly suggests the letters of the painter's name are jumbled

parts.note: ton is an old word for fashion or fashionable style

explanation.surface: A sketch of Paul Klee's surreal, modish manner of painting.
explanation.walkthrough: Ton is an old borrowing from French for the fashionable world or its style.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton is a basic framework or outline, as in a skeleton plan.

clue.text: It helps Browning saluting on behalf of king

parts.note: toasting someone salutes them with raised glasses
for means on behalf of
K is the chess and cards abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Something assists the poet Browning while raising a glass to the king.
explanation.walkthrough: Browning looks like the poet Robert or Elizabeth; here it is making bread brown before a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A toasting fork is a long-handled fork for holding bread to a fire until it is browned.

clue.text: Second mole eating daughter's creepy-crawly

indicators.note: the word for mole eats, takes in, the daughter letter

parts.note: a mole is a breakwater or pier

explanation.surface: Another burrowing mole eats a girl's pet bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' looks like the animal; it is a stone pier or harbour wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider is an eight-legged arachnid, informally a creepy-crawly.

clue.text: Concerned with tense series of courses

parts.note: re means regarding, concerned with
the past is a grammatical tense

explanation.surface: Anxious about a nervous run of lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courses' suggests education; here they are the dishes of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a meal, made up of a series of dishes.

clue.text: Urge lady of the house to scrap first two tablets

indicators.note: the two tablets are scrapped, thrown out of the word for the lady

parts.note: a peeress may sit in the House of Lords
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet; the first two Es in the word are taken

explanation.surface: Encouraging the housewife to give up her pills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady of the house' suggests a housewife; the house is the House of Lords, so she is a PEERESS. E (ecstasy) is a tablet; lose the first two of her three Es.
explanation.definitionFit: To press someone is to urge them strongly to do something.

clue.text: A Republican ready with large cold port

parts.note: ready (or readies) is slang for cash, and so is change
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A Republican prepared with a large, chilly glass of fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold' wants to be C; it belongs to the definition, since Archangel is an Arctic port.
explanation.definitionFit: Archangel (Arkhangelsk) is a Russian port on the White Sea, icebound for much of the year.

clue.text: Doctor abandons fight with current mammal

indicators.note: the doctor leaves the word for fight

parts.note: combat is a fight
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A medic leaves a scrap with an electrified beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A coati is a raccoon-like animal of the Americas with a long snout.

clue.text: Current game finishes early

indicators.note: the name of the game stops before its last letter

parts.note: draughts is the board game called checkers in America

explanation.surface: A match of the moment that ends ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A draught is a current of air, such as one blowing under a door.

clue.text: Draw a time-consuming flyer

indicators.note: the word for flyer eats up, or contains, the letter for time

parts.note: a tract is a pamphlet, a handbill or flyer

explanation.surface: Sketching a pilot who takes ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' suggests a bird or aviator, but it is a printed leaflet.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a crowd is to attract it, pull it in by appeal.

clue.text: Trio's playing beside small lake that has a spit

indicators.note: the three musicians playing makes their letters move about

parts.note: taken as written: the letters of trio plus s
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A musical trio performing by a little lake where there's a spit of land.
explanation.walkthrough: A spit sounds like a geographical sandbar by the lake; here it is a rod for roasting meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotisserie is a cooking device with a rotating skewer on which meat roasts.

clue.text: Indicate area circled by hands

indicators.note: the area letter is surrounded by the word for hands

parts.note: hands are workers, men

explanation.surface: Pointing to a zone ringed by workers.
explanation.definitionFit: To mean something is to signify or indicate it.
